name: Voyager 1
objective: Grand tour of Jupiter and Saturn, followed by an extended mission into interstellar space.
status_note: HISTORICAL / CONCEPTUAL PATH — not a live tracked position.
discoveries: Active volcanoes on Io, detailed views of Saturn's rings, and the first human-made object to enter interstellar space.

journey.discovery: Begins its grand tour trajectory using gravity assists.
Discovered active volcanoes on the moon Io — the first found beyond Earth.
Detailed imaging of Saturn's rings and moon Titan.
Captured Earth as a single pixel from roughly 6 billion km away.
Became the first spacecraft to cross into the interstellar medium.
Still transmitting data over 45+ years after launch.

name: Voyager 2
objective: The only spacecraft to visit Uranus and Neptune, using a rare planetary alignment for a grand tour.
status_note: HISTORICAL / CONCEPTUAL PATH — not a live tracked position.
discoveries: The only close-up data we have of Uranus and Neptune, including their rings, moons, and magnetic fields.

journey.discovery: Launched slightly before Voyager 1, on a slower trajectory to reach all four giant planets.
Additional imaging of Jupiter's atmosphere and moons.
Further ring and moon observations.
First and only close-up look at Uranus, its rings, and its moons.
Discovered active geysers on Neptune's moon Triton.
Became the second human-made object to reach interstellar space.

name: New Horizons
objective: First mission to explore Pluto and the Kuiper Belt up close.
status_note: HISTORICAL / CONCEPTUAL PATH — not a live tracked position.
discoveries: The first detailed images of Pluto and Charon, revealing the heart-shaped Tombaugh Regio.

journey.discovery: Fastest spacecraft launch speed at the time.
Used Jupiter's gravity to boost speed toward Pluto.
First close-up images of Pluto and its moon Charon.
Most distant object ever explored up close at the time.
Continues studying the outer Solar System environment.

name: Juno
objective: Studies Jupiter's composition, gravity field, magnetic field, and polar magnetosphere from orbit.
status_note: HISTORICAL / CONCEPTUAL PATH — not a live tracked position.
discoveries: Revealed complex cyclones at Jupiter's poles and new data on its deep atmosphere and interior.

journey.discovery: Solar-powered — the first mission to the outer planets to rely on solar panels instead of nuclear power.
Entered a highly elliptical polar orbit for close passes over the cloud tops.
Now also studying several of Jupiter's large moons during close flybys.

name: Cassini-Huygens
objective: Studied Saturn, its rings, and its moons; the Huygens probe landed on Titan.
discoveries: Found geysers on Enceladus, mapped Titan's methane lakes, and revealed fine structure in Saturn's rings.

journey.discovery: Began a seven-year cruise to Saturn.
Began 13 years of close-up study of the Saturn system.
First landing on a moon in the outer Solar System.
Discovered active water-ice geysers erupting from the south pole.
Mission ended by design to protect potentially habitable moons from contamination.

name: Parker Solar Probe
objective: Flies closer to the Sun than any spacecraft before it, studying the solar corona and solar wind directly.
status_note: HISTORICAL / CONCEPTUAL PATH — not a live tracked position.
discoveries: Directly sampled the Sun's corona for the first time and studied the origins of the solar wind up close.

journey.discovery: Named after solar physicist Eugene Parker, who predicted the solar wind.
Uses Venus's gravity repeatedly to tighten its orbit closer to the Sun.
Became the first spacecraft to 'touch' the Sun, flying through its outer atmosphere.

name: Hubble Space Telescope
objective: A space-based observatory studying the universe across visible, ultraviolet, and near-infrared light.
status_note: HISTORICAL / CONCEPTUAL PATH — not a live tracked position.
discoveries: Helped determine the rate of the universe's expansion, imaged distant galaxies, and captured iconic nebula imagery.

journey.discovery: Deployed with a flawed mirror, initially producing blurry images.
Astronauts installed corrective optics, fixing the mirror flaw.
A single deep exposure revealed thousands of previously unseen distant galaxies.
Continues operating alongside JWST, over three decades after launch.

name: James Webb Space Telescope
objective: An infrared observatory studying the earliest galaxies, star formation, and exoplanet atmospheres.
status: Active — at the Sun-Earth L2 point
status_note: HISTORICAL / CONCEPTUAL PATH — not a live tracked position.
discoveries: Imaged some of the most distant known galaxies and analyzed exoplanet atmospheric compositions.

journey.discovery: Launched folded up inside a rocket fairing, then unfolded over two weeks in space.
Reached its stable observing position roughly 1.5 million km from Earth.
Revealed the deepest infrared image of the universe taken at the time.
Actively analyzing exoplanet atmospheres and the early universe.
